introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory to all candidates) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The mass, in kilograms, of 100 pigs during a certain period were recorded as follows:

| Mass ($kg$) | 5 - 9 | 10 - 14 | 15 - 19 | 20 - 24 | 25 - 29 | 30 - 34 | 35 - 39 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 25 | 34 | 15 | 13 | 6 | 4 |
incertitudes: Q12(a) : l'histogramme est a tracer par le candidat ; le corrige donne les limites de classes (4,5 a 39,5), les densites de frequence et la marche a suivre. Les classes ayant toutes la meme largeur 5, hauteur = frequence acceptable.
Q12(c) : ecart-type de la population (diviseur 100) = 7,12 kg ; avec le diviseur n - 1 on aurait 7,15 kg. Le sujet ne precise pas ; le programme Additional Maths utilise la formule de la population.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Draw a histogram of the distribution. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This question asks for a drawing; here is exactly what to draw.

**Class boundaries.** The masses are recorded to the nearest kilogram, so the class $5-9$ really covers $4.5\le m<9.5$, and so on. All classes have width $5$, so the frequency density (frequency $\div$ width) is proportional to the frequency, and the bar heights can be the frequencies themselves (or the densities, as in the table).

| Class boundaries | $4.5-9.5$ | $9.5-14.5$ | $14.5-19.5$ | $19.5-24.5$ | $24.5-29.5$ | $29.5-34.5$ | $34.5-39.5$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | $3$ | $25$ | $34$ | $15$ | $13$ | $6$ | $4$ |
| Frequency density (per kg) | $0.6$ | $5$ | $6.8$ | $3$ | $2.6$ | $1.2$ | $0.8$ |

**Drawing.** Choose a scale, for example $1$ cm for $5$ kg on the horizontal axis (starting at $4.5$) and $1$ cm for $5$ units of frequency on the vertical axis (labelled "Frequency"). Draw seven rectangles with **no gaps**, each $1$ cm wide (from $4.5$ to $39.5$), of heights $3,\ 25,\ 34,\ 15,\ 13,\ 6,\ 4$. Label the axes ("Mass (kg)" and "Frequency") and give the histogram a title. The tallest bar is over $14.5-19.5$.
themes: histogram and mode of grouped data

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Hence or otherwise, find the mode. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The modal class is the class with the highest frequency: $15-19$ (frequency $34$), with boundaries $14.5-19.5$.

**Calculation.** Mode $=L+\dfrac{\Delta_1}{\Delta_1+\Delta_2}\times c$, where $L=14.5$ is the lower boundary of the modal class, $c=5$ is the class width, $\Delta_1=34-25=9$ (modal frequency minus the frequency before) and $\Delta_2=34-15=19$ (modal frequency minus the frequency after):

$$\text{Mode}=14.5+\frac{9}{9+19}\times5=14.5+\frac{45}{28}=14.5+1.607\approx16.1.$$

**Graphically:** in the tallest bar, join the top left corner to the top right corner of the neighbouring bar on the left, and the top right corner to the top left corner of the neighbouring bar on the right; the two lines cross above $x\approx16.1$.

**The mode is about $16.1$ kg.**
themes: histogram and mode of grouped data
